record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.original_question: Obtain Littlewood–Richardson rules for the superspace structure constants c^Γ_{ΛΩ} and c̄^Γ_{ΛΩ} defined by the products s_Γ s_Ω = Σ_Λ c^Λ_{ΓΩ} s_Λ and s̄_Γ s̄_Ω = Σ_Λ c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} s̄_Λ, equivalently describing the generalized Littlewood–Richardson coefficients that govern skew Schur functions in superspace.

evidence.quote: Define c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c^Λ_{ΓΩ} to be respectively such that (6.26) s̄_Γ s̄_Ω = ∑_Λ c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} s̄_Λ and s_Γ s_Ω = ∑_Λ c^Λ_{ΓΩ} s_Λ.
Proposition 6.6 – We have (6.27) s_{Λ/Ω} = ∑_Γ c̄^{Λ'}_{Γ'Ω'} s_Γ and s̄_{Λ/Ω} = ∑_Γ c^Λ_{ΩΓ} s̄_Γ.
Open problem 6.7 – An interesting problem would be to obtain Littlewood-Richardson rules for the coefficients c^Γ_{ΛΩ}, c̄^Γ_{ΛΩ}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Symmetric functions in superspace are polynomials in two sets of variables: commuting variables x_1, x_2, ... and anticommuting (Grassmann) variables θ_1, θ_2, ... (with θ_i θ_j = -θ_j θ_i, in particular θ_i^2 = 0), which are simultaneously invariant under the diagonal action of the symmetric group permuting the indices i. A superpartition Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s) consists of a strict partition Λ^a (the "fermionic" part, indexing the θ-variables) together with an ordinary partition Λ^s (the "bosonic" part). 

In the algebra of symmetric functions in superspace there are two natural one-parameter-free families of Schur-like bases indexed by superpartitions, denoted {s_Λ} and {s̄_Λ}. Define the structure constants c^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} by the multiplication rules
   s_Γ · s_Ω = Σ_Λ c^Λ_{ΓΩ} s_Λ,    s̄_Γ · s̄_Ω = Σ_Λ c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} s̄_Λ,
where the sums run over superpartitions Λ. The skew Schur superfunctions s_{Λ/Ω} and s̄_{Λ/Ω} are defined dually and satisfy
   s_{Λ/Ω} = Σ_Γ c̄^{Λ'}_{Γ'Ω'} s_Γ,    s̄_{Λ/Ω} = Σ_Γ c^Λ_{ΩΓ} s̄_Γ,
where Λ' denotes the conjugate superpartition.

Problem. Provide a combinatorial Littlewood–Richardson rule, in the spirit of the classical Littlewood–Richardson rule for Schur functions, that computes the superspace structure constants c^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} as nonnegative (or otherwise explicitly described) integers counting combinatorial objects (such as suitably defined skew tableaux on superpartitions satisfying lattice/Yamanouchi-type conditions).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for Littlewood–Richardson rules for Schur functions in superspace did not surface a published combinatorial rule for the structure constants c^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ}. While LR rules are known for many generalizations (Schur Q-functions, factorial Schur, etc.), no authoritative source was found establishing such a rule for the superspace Schur bases, so the status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Littlewood–Richardson rule - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Describes classical LR rule and known generalizations; no superspace LR rule listed.
status_evidence.claim: No superspace LR rule is documented among standard generalizations.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic formulas for the structure constants in symmetric functions
status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic formulas for structure constants in classical symmetric function bases.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats algebraic structure constants but not the superspace Schur LR rule.
